titleStmt.title: Decree No. 278 of the 14th of June, 1882, declaring Livingston, Guatemala, a free port for ten years from 1st of January, 1883.

div.head: Decree No. 278 of the 14th of June, 1882, declaring Livingston, Guatemala, a free port for ten years from 1st of January, 1883.
div.p: J. Rufino Barrios, general of division and constitutional President of the Republic of Guatemala, considering that the opening of Livingston as a free port of deposit will give impulse in a notable manner to the commercial interests of the country, and will directly and efficiently stimulate the development of the wealth of the fertile coasts of the Atlantic, in use of the powers with which I am invested, I decree:.

From the 1st of January next (1883) the port of Livingston shall be free for importations. On no articles imported thereat, whether for local consumption or for warehousing, shall any maritime duty be imposed during the term of ten years.
The Treasury Department shall designate the zone over which the concessions of the present decree shall be extended, and shall dictate all the regulations for its execution.
Therefore, let it be published for its promulgation and observance, and let account thereof be duly given to the legislative assembly.

closer.dateline: Given in the palace of the executive power in Guatemala the 14th day of June, 1882.
